title: KV: slot-rotor allocator and spill smoother with adaptive pager and frag-score feedback
author: Maya Chen
description:
Context: We continue to see tail-latency spikes during tenant churn and bursty access patterns caused by KV cache fragmentation and hotspot reallocation. The existing slab allocator biases recently-written slots and can create micro-hotspots; when combined with spillover to disk the serving scheduler experiences jitter that propagates into continuous batching windows.

Motivation: Reduce fragmentation-driven stalls and smooth spillback to disk while preserving low-latency for hot prefixes. Provide a feedback signal (frag-score) into the request scheduler so batching and prefetch decisions are aware of memory health. This PR implements a new slot-rotor allocation strategy, a soft-spillback controller ("spill smoother"), and an adaptive pager that uses frag-score telemetry to proactively page cold segments.

What this changes (high level):
- slot-rotor allocator: rotates allocation hotspots across slab lanes per-tenant so long-lived writes don't permanently pin a small set of slots; reduces local fragmentation and evictor thrashing.
- frag-score telemetry: per-tenant fragmentation metric (0..100) computed from occupancy variance, free-run lengths, and eviction churn; exposed to runtime and scheduler.
- spill smoother: rate-limited, token-bucket-based soft spillback that prevents sudden mass-eviction waves; adds hysteresis to avoid oscillation.
- adaptive pager: background paging worker uses frag-score and access heat to proactively write cold pages to spill files under controlled IO budgets; includes paged-prefetch hints for the KV hot-path.
- scheduler integration: batching windows consult frag-score to bias small-window routing away from heavily fragmented shards and to trigger conservative batching when spill risk is high.

Small illustrative snippet (slot rotor rotation logic):
for (auto &lane : slab_lanes) {
    // rotate the starting offset per-tenant to avoid fixed hotspots
    lane.start_offset = (lane.start_offset + tenant_rotation_step(tenant_id)) % lane.capacity;
}

Notes on backwards compatibility: All components are behind the runtime feature-flag `kv.slot_rotor.enabled` (default=false). On upgrade, evictor continues to support previous slab layout; the frag-score defaults to 0 when telemetry is unavailable so scheduler behavior matches legacy paths.

Bench results (selected):
- steady-state: +2.4% throughput on mixed read/write workloads; P50 latency unchanged, P99 down 8% in heavy churn scenarios.
- churn test (10k tenants, periodic hotspot rotation): P95 reduced by 12% and eviction churn reduced by 26%.
- IO: adaptive pager kept background IO under 20% budget; spill smoother reduced simultaneous spill writers by 60%.

Review summary and discussion (single string below includes reviewer comments and responses):
- Arjun: "Nice approach to spread hotspots — can we quantify the extra pointer chasing introduced by rotation?"
  - Maya: "Measured pointer overhead ~0.6% CPU in microbench; amortized by fewer expensive evictions. Added bench `slot-rotor-pointer-overhead` and documented in results."
- Lena: "What happens on tenant deletion where rotation offsets might point into freed slabs?"
  - Maya: "Allocator zeroes rotation state on tenant teardown; added guard checks and a test (slot_rotor_teardown)."
- Diego: "Scheduler hook looks promising but we should avoid thrashing with rapid frag-score changes."
  - Maya: "Added exponential smoothing (alpha=0.15) to frag-score and hysteresis for scheduler triggers; details in frag_score.cpp comments."

CI: build passed, unit tests passed, integration stress bench passed with nominal flakiness tolerance. One flaky test (`kv_eviction_recovery_test`) was rerun and passed on second run. Bench jobs reported improved P99 tail for churn scenario; performance regression job shows no regression on the main steady-state suite.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged after approvals (Arjun, Lena) and bench signoff. Release notes: "Introduces experimental slot-rotor allocator, spill smoother, and adaptive pager to reduce KV cache fragmentation and spill-induced latency spikes. Feature is behind a flag and disabled by default."
